races.name: Meath Farm Machinery Claiming Race

runners_data.name: Alex Belardo
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner under Donagh O'Connor for John McConnell, wearing a visor for the first time; sole career win came over this trip but sim-going record on Good reads 0 wins from 15 attempts, which is a notable concern if he has to battle Hexagonal for the lead from the off.

runners_data.name: Annacroft
runners_data.note: An unusual entry with an OR of 120 in a low-grade claimer and only one run to his name — a distant ninth over 13 furlongs on Soft — making his style, form, and suitability for this mile on Good highly uncertain; Siobhan Rutledge takes the ride.

runners_data.name: Gloriously Glam
runners_data.note: Prominent-racing four-year-old with three wins and four places from 15 runs on Good ground, well placed with Leigh Roche in the saddle; trainer Adrian McGuinness is 3/27 over 14 days and the horse has form at this trip, making it one of the better-credentialed hold-up-adjacent profiles in the field.

runners_data.name: Hexagonal
runners_data.note: The second confirmed front-runner, carrying tongue-tie and hood for Denis Hogan with apprentice Keithen Kennedy aboard; the sim-going record on Good shows 0 wins from 11 tries and recent form figures of 9-9 suggest he may set the pace but be vulnerable late.

runners_data.name: Minaun View
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer who has finished second twice from midfield positions over seven furlongs on soft, running only two days ago which is an unusual prep; tongue-tie and hood in use, and Adrian McGuinness double-stacks with Gloriously Glam in the same race.

runners_data.name: Smithfield
runners_data.note: Prominent-style runner for Gavin Cromwell who wears blinkers and whose recent form includes a 4th in a modest handicap on Good; six runs on Good show 0 wins and 1 place but he usually occupies a handy position and Robert Whearty could find space in a strong-pace scenario.

runners_data.name: Buttermere Ridge
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type flagged as fading in finishes, with a poor sim-going record of 0/15 on Good; the trip is likely short of what Oliver McKiernan's horse now wants given a recent run over 16 furlongs, and the fade flag makes late heroics unlikely.

runners_data.name: Dynamic Force
runners_data.note: Hold-up handler who ran only yesterday, carrying no headgear; the sim-going record on Good is weak at 0/15 but he has two places and is consistent enough to be involved if the pace is truly honest, though running on consecutive days is a concern.

runners_data.name: Land Of The Giants
runners_data.note: Rory Cleary partners this four-year-old who won over nine furlongs on Good and has placed twice on similar ground; a 35-day break is manageable, the hold-up style suits a well-run mile, and the McGuinness yard adding a third runner underlines confidence — this profile makes most sense in a truly run race.

runners_data.name: Rampage
runners_data.note: Prominent-style runner with a fading form line of 086700 and a weak sim-going record; T G McCourt's seven-year-old is ridden by a 7lb claimer and the headgear combination of tongue-tie and visor hasn't produced a win in 15 Good-ground attempts.

runners_data.name: Colugo
runners_data.note: Ian Donoghue's five-year-old is a genuine hold-up horse — last five runs include trips of 9f to 18f — placed here in midfield on the map purely because the field is saturated with rear-runners; racing at a mile for the first time and out of natural role, the STYLE_FIT discount of 0.90 applies and his chance is tempered accordingly.

runners_data.name: Je Suis Celebre
runners_data.note: Unclassified style type for Stephen Thorne who has two placed runs from five on similar ground and wears tongue-tie and hood; a 36-day break and a step back from ten furlongs to a mile might not be ideal, but the four previous Good-ground runs give some going confidence.

runners_data.name: Lohengrin
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse whose last four completed starts on Good ground read 10th, 11th, 14th, 20th — a deeply concerning profile; placed in midfield on the map because of field congestion at the rear, not because of his running style, and the fade flag combined with a STYLE_FIT discount makes this a very difficult win scenario.

runners_data.name: Tara Na Ri
runners_data.note: Noel Meade's four-year-old ran only two days ago and fades in finishes; the form figures of 8-0050 over eight-to-ten furlongs on Good are modest, and racing from a hold-up position in a field this size with a fade tendency makes a win unlikely.

runners_data.name: Countertop
runners_data.note: A two-year-old with an OR of 120 and a form line of 0700— after 260 days off the track; Terry Casey's 7lb claim eases the weight but the layoff, the age profile, and the fade flag make this an extreme outsider in a competitive 17-runner claiming race.

runners_data.name: Mullacash Buzz
runners_data.note: Thomas Dowling's eight-year-old has placed twice from five Good-ground outings and runs with a tongue-tie and hood; prominent style suits a race where pace is hot, and while the OR of 40 reflects modest ability, the consistent prominent positioning at this trip means he may stay involved longer than expected.

runners_data.name: Wonderwalk
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse whose last five runs are all at 10-to-18 furlongs — this mile trip is a sharp drop in distance; pushed into midfield on the map because the field's rear is overcrowded, not by inclination, and the fade flag plus STYLE_FIT discount of 0.90 make this a very unlikely winner at the mile trip.

races.paceDynamic: Alex Belardo and Hexagonal are the two confirmed front-runners and will clash for the early lead in a 17-runner field, creating a genuinely contested pace from the outset on Good turf at Bellewstown over a mile. With both committed to forcing the pace, neither is likely to give ground cheaply, meaning the gallop should be honest-to-strong rather than falsely run, and the race will be set up from the front with limited respite for those tracking. Gloriously Glam, Smithfield, Minaun View, Mullacash Buzz, and Rampage all want prominent positions, intensifying the early battle and compressing the midfield; Land Of The Giants, Dynamic Force, and the redistributed hold-up types will be shuffled back further than ideal. This race shape — two genuine front-runners fighting it out in a large, pace-heavy field — strongly favours horses who can track just off the pressure from a handy position and sustain their effort through the final two furlongs, giving the edge to prominent-to-midfield closers with proven Good-ground form over a mile.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Prominent Stalker Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Alex Belardo and Hexagonal duel for the lead and their battle burns them out in the final furlong, a prominent tracker sitting just behind the speed pounces.
scenarios.body: If Alex Belardo and Hexagonal duel for the lead and their battle burns them out in the final furlong, a prominent tracker sitting just behind the speed pounces.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Survives Contested Duel
scenarios.trigger: If one of the front-runners — most likely Alex Belardo — controls the pace cleverly enough to avoid a true war and steals a march at the top of the straight.
scenarios.body: If one of the front-runners — most likely Alex Belardo — controls the pace cleverly enough to avoid a true war and steals a march at the top of the straight.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Closer Sweeps Through
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runners set a truly scorching pace that burns off all prominent types, creating a vacuum for a strong mid-division finisher to sweep past.
scenarios.body: If the front-runners set a truly scorching pace that burns off all prominent types, creating a vacuum for a strong mid-division finisher to sweep past.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: True Hold-Up Horses Finish Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so strong it collapses the entire field and the deepest-sitting horses are able to thread through late — a scenario that depends on redistributed types finding unobstructed ground.
scenarios.body: If the pace is so strong it collapses the entire field and the deepest-sitting horses are able to thread through late — a scenario that depends on redistributed types finding unobstructed ground.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Alex Belardo or Hexagonal wins the early argument for the lead — if Hexagonal sets a suicidal gallop trying to make all, the race could turn into a procession for anything tracking just off them at the top of the straight.

Land Of The Giants is 35 days off the track and must negotiate a 17-runner field from a hold-up position — if she gets a clean passage off the strong pace she is the most interesting off-the-pace profile, but traffic at Bellewstown over a mile is a real risk.

Adrian McGuinness runs three horses (Gloriously Glam, Minaun View, Land Of The Giants) — watch for any stable drift or market move that identifies which runner the yard is targeting, as all three have different pace profiles that could affect how they're deployed.

Countertop — a two-year-old returning after 260 days — is worth monitoring in the early market; any late withdrawal or unusual market movement could reshuffle the pace dynamics if any of the confirmed front-runners are affected.

Dynamic Force and Rampage both ran within the last 24 hours — quick back-to-back runners in claiming company can be vulnerable, but if either comes out fresh and well, their handling of Good ground is worth noting given the race's honesty of pace.

races.name: Irish EBF Median Sires Series (C & G) Maiden
Smiths Of Drogheda Ford Classic Handicap

runners_data.name: Lahore Da King
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner in this field, wearing a tongue-plate and ridden by a 7lb claimer; best recent form came winning on Soft over 8f, and the step back to Good ground here shows 0W0P in similar conditions — pace tactics are key but the lack of similar-going wins tempers expectations.

runners_data.name: Zipster
runners_data.note: Prominent racer returning after 79 days off for Gerard O'Leary, with two places from seven runs on comparable Going and a solid profile at 8f; Dylan Browne McMonagle is a significant jockey booking that upgrades the chance considerably from the ratings alone.

runners_data.name: Kitty Bear
runners_data.note: Two wins in recent form including a 8f Good-ground success, making her one of the better Going-suited horses in the field; Orla Tynan's 7lb claim keeps the weight competitive and the trainer's recent 2/29 form is active — a genuine prominent type who should get her position here.

runners_data.name: Bucaneer's Spirit
runners_data.note: Gary Carroll takes over on a horse with an outstanding record — 2W4P from 12 runs on Good ground — making him the most course-going-specific runner in the race; prominent style suits the likely race shape and the 15-day turnaround with a fresh win last time out signals readiness.

runners_data.name: Darkdeserthighway
runners_data.note: Colin Keane is a significant positive booking for a hold-up type who has placed twice in seven Good-ground runs and is stepping back in trip from recent Standside-rail handicaps; blinkers applied and 112 days off could mean freshness or rustiness — needs a proper pace to deliver late.

runners_data.name: Free Solo
runners_data.note: A genuine front-runner by nature who has been mapped to midfield given the crowded prominent zone — 2W2P over 7f on Good and wears a tongue-plate; at age nine with Chris Hayes aboard, the ability to secure a forward pitch will determine whether the rating can be exploited.

runners_data.name: Gotta Catch'em All
runners_data.note: Siobhan Rutledge rides a horse who has shown placing form on Good ground but mostly at 10f — dropping to a mile is the question, and no wins or places in last six starts makes this a speculative each-way proposition at best.

runners_data.name: Comfort Line
runners_data.note: A true prominent type who may not get that berth in this crowded field, wearing a visor for Adrian McGuinness who is in decent recent form (3/20 in 14 days); the horse has placed three times on Good ground and a recent second over 7f Good suggests the conditions suit, but position is the variable.

runners_data.name: Bay Of Dreams
runners_data.note: Ben Coen, an elite jockey booking, is the eye-catching angle for this Ben Coen–Ciaran Murphy combination; naturally prominent but likely to be shuffled back in this field, the horse has placed six times in 13 Good-ground runs and beat rivals at 9f — dropping in trip is a minor query.

runners_data.name: Variance
runners_data.note: Three-year-old returning after 233 days off for the British-trained Newland/Insole yard — an unusually long layoff raises a significant fitness question; hold-up style needs a pace scenario that may not materialise, and the limited Good-going sample makes assessment difficult.

runners_data.name: Rockbury Lad
runners_data.note: Flagged as a horse that fades in finishes and a hold-up type mapped to midfield given the congested rear; Jamie Powell rides a seven-year-old wearing a tongue-plate who has failed to place in last four and shows 1W1P from 10 Good-ground starts — the finishing pattern is a genuine concern in any scenario.

runners_data.name: Glamazon
runners_data.note: Shane Foley rides a three-year-old for the Harrington yard who has a win over 10f Good recently and blinkers applied; dropping back to a mile and taking on older handicappers is the test, but Foley's presence and the trainer's 5/29 form rate (in 14 days) suggest stable confidence.

runners_data.name: Imnotleavinyou
runners_data.note: Ran just two days ago and wears a hood — the quick turnaround is noted, but this hold-up type has three wins and two places from nine Good-ground starts and won over 7f Good recently; Declan McDonogh is a strong booking and this horse's condition record suggests connections are not afraid of short intervals.

runners_data.name: Smaoineamh Sile
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old hold-up type flagged for fading in finishes, returning after 171 days off on Standside ground with a 0W0P record on Good — this is one of the weakest profiles in the race and the layoff combined with the finishing tendency makes it hard to construct a winning scenario.

runners_data.name: Tariff
runners_data.note: Two-year-old (likely a three-year-old based on form) returning after 198 days off for the McGuinness yard, with a limited all-Standside form profile showing no wins; hold-up style, long layoff, and inexperience at this level make this a very unexposed entry that needs substantial improvement on known form.

races.paceDynamic: Lahore Da King is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no natural rival prepared to press from the gates, should dictate an uncontested, controlled tempo around Bellewstown's tight turning track. The critical complication is that Free Solo, Comfort Line, and Bay Of Dreams are all genuine prominent types who cannot all secure their preferred positions — one or two will be forced to either push up and create pressure or drop back and race against their nature, with Lahore Da King and Zipster or Kitty Bear most likely to occupy the real front slots. On Good ground over a mile at a track that rewards position and rail-hugging, a steady-to-moderate pace set by Lahore Da King will compress the field and reduce the advantage of true hold-up runners, giving those able to track close and sustain their effort through the turn every advantage. This race shape strongly favours prominent, on-pace stalkers who can sit just off the leader and pounce in the straight — deep closers relying on a strong pace to pull them through will be left wanting.

scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Stalkers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Lahore Da King dictates a measured pace unchallenged and prominent trackers Zipster, Kitty Bear, or Bucaneer's Spirit settle just behind.
scenarios.body: If Lahore Da King dictates a measured pace unchallenged and prominent trackers Zipster, Kitty Bear, or Bucaneer's Spirit settle just behind.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Injection Mid-Race
scenarios.trigger: If one or more of the redistributed prominent types — Free Solo, Comfort Line, or Bay Of Dreams — pushes forward aggressively after the early stages and lifts the tempo.
scenarios.body: If one or more of the redistributed prominent types — Free Solo, Comfort Line, or Bay Of Dreams — pushes forward aggressively after the early stages and lifts the tempo.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is slow enough that the field bunches and multiple horses surge late, making this a sprint finish from 3f out.
scenarios.body: If the early pace is slow enough that the field bunches and multiple horses surge late, making this a sprint finish from 3f out.

scenarios.title: Front Runner Defies
scenarios.trigger: If Lahore Da King, left completely alone in front, bowls along at a perfectly judged pace and simply isn't caught.
scenarios.body: If Lahore Da King, left completely alone in front, bowls along at a perfectly judged pace and simply isn't caught.

watchPoints.text: Bucaneer's Spirit has the strongest Going-specific profile in the race (2W4P on Good) and Gary Carroll will ensure he gets his natural prominent pitch — any market drift should be taken seriously given the stats.

Free Solo, Comfort Line, and Bay Of Dreams cannot all race prominently — watch the early exchanges closely to see which one is forced back, as the displaced horse's chance is materially reduced regardless of form.

Imnotleavinyou ran only two days ago; if Declan McDonogh produces a positive ride from the hold-up position this horse is clearly fresh enough, but a flat performance would be explained by the short turnaround.

Variance (233 days off) and Smaoineamh Sile (171 days off) are both returning from extended breaks — if either shows market support on-course, it would be significant insider news given the lack of recent racecourse evidence.

Dylan Browne McMonagle's booking on Zipster is a clear upgrade in jockey quality for an OR 70 horse at a middle-ranking track — watch if the market reflects that the stable expects a bold show first time back after 79 days.

races.name: Landy, Muldoon & Co Maiden

runners_data.name: Reposado
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who has placed twice on good ground over 6f; dropping back to 5f is a slight unknown but Bellewstown's sharp track suits a horse that travels on the pace, and the 15-day turnaround with Donagh O'Connor aboard is a straightforward booking.

runners_data.name: Banish Misfortune
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner whose lone form line (16th on soft over 7f) is unimpressive, but OR=120 vastly outgrades this field on paper; the key risk is whether she can translate that rating into a genuine winning effort once caught near the line — flagged as a horse who fades in the finish.

runners_data.name: Ennoble
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with Dylan Browne McMonagle, the strongest jockey booking in the race, and a third-place finish on good ground over 5f sitting in the book; the 48-day absence is a mild flag but JP O'Brien's yard runs 16/79 in the T14 window, suggesting the horse is likely tuned up.

runners_data.name: Profit Surge
runners_data.note: Consistent front-to-rear prominent type who has placed three times from 15 runs on good ground; blinkered today, which is a positive headgear flag, and Colin Keane's presence lifts the booking — the step down from 6-7f to 5f is the main query given his best form has come at longer trips.

runners_data.name: Sparky Sparky
runners_data.note: Wears a hood today for the first time, which could sharpen early concentration; has a 2nd over 5f good ground in recent form and JP Murtagh's yard is lightly represented at 2/29 over 14 days — genuine hold-up style that needs others to go hard enough in front.

runners_data.name: Focaccia
runners_data.note: In-form performer who finished 2nd over 5f on standard and 3rd over 6f at Heacock, but her natural hold-up style means she is squeezed into a midfield slot here by field composition rather than preference — the 6-day turnaround is brisk, and her chance is somewhat dependent on the pace truly collapsing.

runners_data.name: Kidd
runners_data.note: Entirely unknown quantity — no public form, unclassified style, apprentice rider Jessica Maye claims 7lb, and John McConnell's yard is 3/16 in the T14 window; the tongue-tie is a headgear debut and the blank form string makes any assessment speculative.

runners_data.name: White Smoke
runners_data.note: Has a career second over 6f on soft and bumped along in midfield on good ground previously; a true hold-up type by profile whose position in this race map is a consequence of field congestion at the rear rather than tactical choice — 55 days off is the most notable flag, and McCullagh will need favours up front.

races.paceDynamic: Banish Misfortune is the confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, should coast across to the rail and dictate a sustainable, uncontested gallop over this 5f trip at Bellewstown. That controlled pace scenario suits a horse who can travel prominently and quicken, rather than those who need a true end-to-end gallop to close into. White Smoke and Focaccia are genuine hold-up types who have been redistributed to midfield on the map because the rear of the field is overcrowded with closers — they are unlikely to secure their natural positions and their chances should be tempered accordingly. The race shape overwhelmingly favours a prominent or pace-tracking profile, with the winner most likely to be sitting just behind Banish Misfortune and kicking off the bend rather than arriving late from the back.

scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Kicks
scenarios.trigger: If Banish Misfortune dictates a steady, uncontested pace and the winner tracks closely throughout.
scenarios.body: If Banish Misfortune dictates a steady, uncontested pace and the winner tracks closely throughout.

scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Banish Misfortune goes off too quickly in a falsely run sense and ties up in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: If Banish Misfortune goes off too quickly in a falsely run sense and ties up in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Honest, All-The-Way Win
scenarios.trigger: If Banish Misfortune finds an extra gear and simply stays on strongly to win from the front.
scenarios.body: If Banish Misfortune finds an extra gear and simply stays on strongly to win from the front.

scenarios.title: Chaos Break, Outsider Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If there is significant early crowding or interference that scrambles the predicted shape entirely.
scenarios.body: If there is significant early crowding or interference that scrambles the predicted shape entirely.

watchPoints.text: Banish Misfortune vs the pace question — if she is allowed to bowl along completely unchallenged, she sets a dangerously comfortable tempo that could deliver a front-running or close-tracking win, so watch how quickly she clears the field in the opening furlong.

Focaccia and White Smoke are genuine closers who cannot realistically get their natural position in this small, pace-light field — if they drift further back than the map suggests, their chances diminish sharply and backers should be aware their redistribution is structural, not cosmetic.

Kidd is a complete unknown with a 7lb claim and a tongue-tie debut — watch the market and paddock behaviour closely as any significant support would represent inside information in a horse with zero public form.

Sparky Sparky's hood application today is worth monitoring in the paddock — if it settles her early, she has the 5f good-ground form (2nd recently) to be competitive, but a fractious pre-race demeanour would undermine her chance significantly.

Profit Surge's blinkered headgear could sharpen his early response and push him closer to Banish Misfortune than his recent trip profile would suggest — monitor whether he contests the lead early, which would change the pace dynamic materially.

races.name: Eco Bullet Handicap (0-60)

runners_data.name: Viamonte
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who has shown fair course form over 5f on good ground (four placings at this trip/going combo), but trainer T Browne has been firing — 1 from 1 in the 14-day window; finishing position from the rear will be difficult in a single-paced race.

runners_data.name: Happy Henry
runners_data.note: The confirmed pace-setter here; McCreery returns him quickly at 9 days and he has the course-and-distance form to match, though the [STYLE_FIT=0.91] flag notes this as slightly out of natural role — his best chance is to exploit the lack of pressure and dictate throughout.

runners_data.name: Bye Bye Now
runners_data.note: Prominent racer returned after a 93-day break; has a course win at 5f on standard but all recent form comes from Standside, and trainer McConnell has 1 from 14 in the 14-day window — fitness after the layoff is the key question.

runners_data.name: Sceitimini
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse flagged for fading in the finish; the 161-day absence is a major concern, and Colin Keane's booking gives it profile, but the form line over 5f on good ground (2 from 5 placements, 0 wins) is not encouraging.

runners_data.name: Dandy Land
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse whose true finishing kick is compromised by the crowded rear of this field; the ⚠ fade flag compounds the problem, and DBM's booking is eyecatching, but the horse's position will be shaped by traffic rather than tactics.

runners_data.name: Plushy
runners_data.note: Three-year-old hold-up type with headgear fitted (hg:h); Cromwell has been in form (7 from 53 over 14 days) and the 26-day gap is fine, but six consecutive out-of-the-frame finishes on good ground make confidence hard to justify.

runners_data.name: Army Leave
runners_data.note: Two-year-old at the time of last run, now returning after 366 days off; going type coded as turf specialist (hg:t), but the near-year absence and apprentice booking mean readiness is a major unknown regardless of style.

runners_data.name: Platino Bianco
runners_data.note: Won last time at 5f on good ground nine days ago — the most recent form clock in the field; true hold-up horse shuffled closer in the map due to field congestion at the rear, but the live winning form and headgear (hg:tv) make it dangerous to dismiss entirely.

runners_data.name: Whatswrongnow
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with a tidy form string (220302) and solid record on good ground (8 from 15 runs, 3 placings); Mulligan claims 5lb and the horse ran just two days ago which merits monitoring, but the style suits a pace-tracking role perfectly here.

runners_data.name: Steel Magnolia
runners_data.note: McCreery's second string in the race, returned nine days ago; hold-up horse placed four times at 5f on good/soft, but the style-fit concern and redistribution mean it will not get the clean run it needs from this packed field.

runners_data.name: Realtin Fantasy
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old hold-up horse off 245 days; has historical placed form at 5f on good ground but the lengthy break, the age, and the trainer's 0/0 14-day record leave little to work with — redistribution away from true rear running compounds the issue.

runners_data.name: Apache Star
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old who has been finishing in the rear of fields (60990 form string) at 5f on good; headgear fitted (hg:tb) but the pattern of double-figure finishes and the style concern mean it is very hard to construct a winning scenario.

runners_data.name: Bel Espoir
runners_data.note: Four-year-old with a concerning form string (-09000) and a ⚠ fade flag; all recent runs have produced double-figure finishes, and while the horse has run at this trip and going, the redistribution away from the rear only moves it into traffic it cannot navigate.

runners_data.name: You Smiled
runners_data.note: Three-year-old with just three career runs (907), all on good or soft over 5-6f; the ⚠ fade flag, the inexperience, and the redistribution away from natural hold-up position mean Tynan's apprentice claim (7lb) is unlikely to compensate for the positional disadvantage.

races.paceDynamic: Happy Henry is the confirmed front-runner and looks set to lead this 14-runner 5f handicap at a sustainable, uncontested pace on good ground at Bellewstown, giving him a clean passage throughout. With no other confirmed pace-setter to pressure him, he should dictate terms comfortably, controlling the tempo from the outset through to the climb to the line. The field is heavily stacked with hold-up types — Dandy Land, Platino Bianco, Steel Magnolia, Realtin Fantasy, Apache Star, Bel Espoir and You Smiled are all genuine closers who cannot all operate from their natural rear position and have been mapped further forward than they will actually race. The race shape heavily favours prominent or pace-tracking runners who can sit just off Happy Henry and pounce in the straight, as the steady gallop set by a lone leader on this flat 5f track will not generate the deep closing run needed for true hold-up horses to reel in the front rank.

scenarios.body: If multiple runners contest the early lead unexpectedly and the gallop becomes ragged, causing a scrambled finish with a wide-open result.

watchPoints.text: Happy Henry — if he crosses cleanly from his draw and hits the front unchallenged inside the first furlong, Leigh Roche can control tempo entirely; any drift or early bump compromises the whole pace map.

Whatswrongnow — ran just two days ago and Rory Mulligan (5lb claim) rides; watch the market and how fresh the horse looks at the start, as a flat-out peak effort this quickly can affect finishing effort.

Platino Bianco — won nine days ago at this exact trip and going; despite redistribution to midfield due to field congestion, it retains live form credentials and could find a run if the pace compresses the field late.

Bye Bye Now — 93-day absence means fitness is unproven; Siobhan Rutledge's booking and the prior course form make it a horse to track in the market, as a market move would signal stable confidence over the layoff concern.

The cluster of redistributed hold-up horses (Dandy Land, Steel Magnolia, Realtin Fantasy, Apache Star, Bel Espoir, You Smiled) will all be seeking to race from positions they cannot naturally claim — watch the first furlong for jostling and potential interference as multiple riders are pushed wider than ideal.

races.name: Dore & Co. Solicitors Handicap (0-60)

runners_data.name: Rising Sky
runners_data.note: The one confirmed front-runner in the race; last won over 10f on standard going and drops back in trip from recent 11f run, but the flat Bellewstown track suits a leader and at OR 60 off 9 days' rest Adam Grant rides claim — the key horse to watch for how aggressively the early pace is set.

runners_data.name: Porsche Lad
runners_data.note: Prominent type who has shown his best form on softer ground (sim-going record 2/15) and has been out 22 days; Conor Cusack claims 7lb but the switch to good going at 1m4f is a question mark and finishing form recently unremarkable.

runners_data.name: Cala Gracioneta
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly with a notable second over 2m on good ground in her history, which is the best same-going evidence in this field over the trip; a fade warning is flagged and Matthew Smith's stable is 0/9 in 14 days, so confidence is tempered.

runners_data.name: Robot Rock
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with a positive second on Tapeta and modest good-ground record (3/5 sim-going, 0W); the fade warning and a 23-day break under Siobhan Rutledge suggest this is more of a place-at-best contender.

runners_data.name: Jazz Forever
runners_data.note: Genuine stayer who has finished third over 13f on good ground and shown creditable form at 2m-plus; true hold-up style fits this distance but needs a strong pace to deliver, which this race shape may not provide.

runners_data.name: Trishuli River
runners_data.note: Prominent-to-tracking type with a win over 12f on standard and placed form on good — the most credible pace-pressing rival to Rising Sky; Leigh Roche's experience and a solid sim-going record (3/15) give him a legitimate each-way profile if he travels close to the pace.

runners_data.name: Eastern Wind
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse by nature, pushed forward on the map only because the field is so packed with closers; T G McCourt yard is 1/11 in 14 days, and his best two good-ground finishes were second and third over comparable trips — one to watch if gaps appear, but his natural position will be rearward.

runners_data.name: Magna Gee Gee
runners_data.note: OR 54 four-year-old filly without a win in 15 starts; hold-up style and poor sim-going record (4/15, 0W) make her difficult to recommend, and Robyn Donaghue-Leahy's 7lb claim is the main interest.

runners_data.name: Circus Act
runners_data.note: Veteran seven-year-old who has won over good ground (1W in sim-going), but prefers marathon trips (20f history) and is racing here over a much shorter 1m4f; Jack Cleary's 5lb claim helps but the trip reduction is a significant concern, and he's been forced into a midfield map position despite preferring to come from well off the pace.

runners_data.name: Without Love
runners_data.note: Four-year-old who won over 10f on standard going and has placed form at 12f; been off 112 days which is the longest layoff in the field — fitness is the primary question, though the mile-and-a-half trip is well within his comfort zone; a natural hold-up type who arrives in midfield on the map by necessity.

runners_data.name: Sir Trancealot
runners_data.note: Lightly raced three-year-old trained by J P Murtagh (2/24 in 14 days) at OR 59 — the highest OR among the three-year-olds; hold-up in natural style but good-ground form is minimal (2/4 sim-going), and the step up in field size to 19 runners on a tight-ish track requires a clear run.

runners_data.name: Masego
runners_data.note: Won over 13f on good ground last time out and that recent win sets him apart from many in this field; hold-up type who will be at the back and needs gaps — Ms Margaret Mullins' yard is 0/5 in 14 days, and a 49-day break adds a fitness caveat despite the positive form.

runners_data.name: Amethyst Stone
runners_data.note: Three-year-old trained by G M Lyons (9/20 in 14 days, a hot trainer angle) with an OR of 57 but has placed in none of her four good-ground starts — consistent disappointment on the going she faces today; hold-up style needs more pace than Rising Sky is likely to generate.

runners_data.name: Sarmiento Power
runners_data.note: OR 44 with a poor recent string (580000) and a sim-going record of 2/15 with no wins; the fade warning is significant, and while Matthew Smith trains a second runner here, the evidence of ability is limited.

runners_data.name: Idomything
runners_data.note: Placed sixth over 13f on soft last time; his going profile is soft rather than good (most history on soft/yielding) and the switch to good ground is a concern; Thomas Cleary's yard is 0/1 in 14 days and a 13-day turnaround is tight.

runners_data.name: No Bother Aoife
runners_data.note: Gavin Cromwell is a powerful trainer (9/56 in 14 days) which is the standout positive; however, this three-year-old filly is stepping massively up in trip from 7-10f runs and has faded in finish flags — the trainer angle is worth monitoring but the trip and form profile are against her.

runners_data.name: Private Larry
runners_data.note: Has a natural hold-up profile and fades in finish; the form string of 00088 reads poorly and all good-ground runs have returned mid-pack finishes — Alan McIntyre is 0/1 in 14 days and the handicapper has the horse well framed at OR 52 based on limited upside.

runners_data.name: Maker's Mark
runners_data.note: T G McCourt runs a second horse here (alongside Eastern Wind); OR 52 three-year-old with a mostly soft-ground form profile and all good-ground efforts returning mid-field results — Sadhbh Tormey's 7lb claim is the headline, but the trip of 1m4f is further than anything in his form.

runners_data.name: Plus Or Minus
runners_data.note: Form entirely on soft ground (7/13f, 11/12f, 9/12f, 7/12f on soft) with a lone good-ground run returning eighth over 10f — this is the most significant going concern in the field; P A Fahy is 0/6 in 14 days and the switch to good at 1m4f looks unfavourable.

races.paceDynamic: Rising Sky is the sole confirmed front-runner in a field of 19 and should be able to dictate from the front at a controlled, sustainable gallop over 1m4f on good ground at Bellewstown — a flat, straightforward course that does not naturally punish a leader who gets an easy time. Porsche Lad and Trishuli River are the likeliest horses to press from prominent positions, but neither is a natural pace-setter and both are unlikely to seriously challenge Rising Sky's lead, meaning the fractions could be genuinely modest. Eastern Wind, Private Larry, No Bother Aoife, Circus Act, Masego, Without Love, Sarmiento Power, Idomything, Maker's Mark, Plus Or Minus and No Bother Aoife are all true hold-up or midfield types redistributed forward on the map because the field holds more genuine back-of-the-field horses than can realistically race there — Rising Sky, and to a lesser extent Porsche Lad and Trishuli River, are the runners most likely to actually secure early position. The tactical verdict is clear: with one uncontested front-runner setting a modest pace in a wide, flat-track handicap, prominent-to-midfield horses who can travel close to the pace and sustain their effort through the final two furlongs are best placed — true hold-up horses face an additional challenge as there may simply not be enough pace to close into.

watchPoints.text: Rising Sky's early fractions are the key to the entire race shape — if Adam Grant gets a soft lead and the pace collapses below a genuine gallop, the hold-up horses at the rear of this 19-runner field will almost certainly be left with too much ground to make up in the straight.

Eastern Wind and Circus Act are genuine hold-up horses placed in midfield on the map by redistribution — watch whether they actually drop back to their natural position early, because if they do, they will be further back than the map suggests and need a stronger pace than anticipated.

Masego is the one hold-up runner with a recent win on good ground at a comparable trip — if gaps appear in the straight he is the most credibly-form hold-up danger, but a 49-day absence and the need for a strong pace to close into are conditions that must both be met.

Plus Or Minus has run all his form on soft ground — if the going report of Good is accurate throughout the evening at Bellewstown, this runner's chance is materially compromised and the going line from earlier races should be checked before the off.

Trainer G M Lyons (9/20 in 14 days) with Amethyst Stone and J P Murtagh (2/24 in 14 days) with Sir Trancealot represent the two strongest trainer-in-form angles — monitor market movement on both as indicators of stable confidence, even if the raw form profiles are modest.
